summary: I audited the visit → person → lead → follow-up signal and the social feeds, using the schema snapshot, the snapshot cron routes, the client tracking components, site_signal aggregates (SQL early, then the sb.mjs helper after the rule change), the scoreboard probe, a Chrome-UA curl of production, and git history. Long-form notes with every query and row are at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RyanRealty/9fe9d814-a247-5921-8288-dab9436e06db/scratchpad/tracking/notes.md. The crons are alive: snapshot-channels runs 8/8 daily at 12:20Z, GSC/GBP/meta_graph/x/tiktok/youtube account scopes are fresh to 09-19..09-21, email events are minutes old, token heartbeats pass. The stale sources are explained: fub_api_v1 is a decommissioned system whose 1,228 rows still sit in the view; meta_ads_insights_api has written nothing since 2026-06-19 although it is still in the fan-out (children do not log, so ran-but-wrote-zero is invisible); tiktok video and x post are 30-day lookback feeds on idle accounts; ga4 channel scope only writes on days with social sessions. The real defects are in what the numbers mean. (1) GA4 is dominated by a server-side Measurement Protocol page_view mirror added 2026-08-10 in app/api/visitors/track/route.ts:486-565: in 14 days GA4 shows 28,804 page_views but only 370 session_start and 262 first_visit; 8,593 of ~8,900 sessions are source '(not set)', google/organic = 1, bounce_rate 1.0 and engagement_rate 0 on most days. GA4 sessions, engagement, new users, source/medium and lead source are not human truth, and organic → lead attribution in GA4 is impossible. (2) The browser-side GA4 stream (gtag via GTM-WV6R4NZ5) shows the same zero-signature it had during the documented 08-19..08-31 suppression bug again from 2026-09-18 (session_start 1 then absent, new_users 0), right after commit f1e2a90f9 touched GTMHead/GoogleAnalytics/PageViewTracker; the GA4 ingestor pulls yesterday-only with no settle window, and the silent-zero guard keys by channel×metric so a dead event stream can never trip it. A live fire test was blocked by the sandbox proxy. (3) RUM is polluted: /_next/image is the single largest surface (20,306 of 45,354 LCP rows in 14 days) because a missing image URL returns the app's 142 KB not-found page which mounts the vitals reporter and VisitTracker; INP has only 1,394 rows so per-route INP p75 is unusable; no bot filter, no sampling, no path normalization. (4) First-party attribution works for the 1.7% of sessions that carry a referrer, but of 90 people identified in 7 days exactly 1 is attributed to organic search, crm_people stores no channel, the attribution crons only score paid tags, and 98% of sessions are 'direct' with no bot filter and UA stripped at essential tier. (5) GSC is top-25 queries + top-25 pages per day, no page×query, no URL inspection cron, no Bing — you cannot diagnose a per-page ranking loss from it. (6) Speed-to-lead is flagged (11 of the 15 most recent site submits had no human touch in 24 h) but never stored as a metric; SMS consent has no record. Nothing from site_signal, GA4, GSC, RUM or social flows into prioritization automatically; nodes are hand-pasted and COMPANY_SCOREBOARD.md is five weeks stale.

findings.title: GA4 is dominated by server-mirrored page_views, so sessions, engagement, new users and source/medium are not human truth and organic → lead attribution in GA4 is impossible
findings.claim: Since 2026-08-10 /api/visitors/track mirrors every essential-tier page view into GA4 via Measurement Protocol (client_id from rr_session_id, engagement_time_msec 100, no first_visit/session_start, no campaign attribution). In the last 14 days GA4 shows 28,804 page_views vs 370 session_start and 262 first_visit; 8,593 of ~8,900 sessions are source '(not set)', google/organic = 1, lead_source '(not set)' 156/161, bounce_rate 1.0 and engagement_rate 0 on most days. The GA4 numbers the loop, the scoreboard and the growth measurer read are fabricated by our own server, not measured behavior.
findings.evidence: app/api/visitors/track/route.ts:486-565; lib/ga4-measurement-protocol.ts:171-234; site_signal ga4_data_api 14d: event sums page_view 28,804 / session_start 370 / first_visit 262; account sessions 8,743; source scope '(not set)' 8,593, 'google / organic' 1; lead_source '(not set)' 156 of 161; daily bounce_rate 1.0 / engagement_rate 0 on 09-13 and 09-18..09-21 (ga4-daily-series.txt).
findings.why_it_matters: Every 'organic sessions', 'conversion rate' and 'lead source' figure read from GA4 for the be-seen → convert mission is wrong by construction; GA4 cannot tell Matt whether search or AI traffic converts, and any accept test written against GA4 sessions or lead_event_rate measures the mirror, not people.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the page_view/listing_view mirror (keep MP only for post-success conversion events that carry a real _ga client id, and send session_id/engagement correctly for those). Declare visitor_sessions/visitor_events the traffic source of record for the scoreboard, and re-point the GA4 ingestor's account rows to gtag-only measures (session_start-based) or drop them from site_signal. Update docs/TRACKING_POLICY.md and the loop's ingest list to say GA4 is a ≤4% consented sample plus conversions, not traffic.

findings.title: Browser-side GA4 stream has been at zero since 2026-09-18 (same signature as the confirmed 08-19..08-31 tag bug) and no guard can see it
findings.claim: gtag-only events (session_start, first_visit, user_engagement) fell to 1 on 09-18 and are absent 09-19..09-21 while MP page_views continue — the exact signature of the documented GTM load-suppression bug (08-19..08-31, fixed 09-01). It coincides with f1e2a90f9 (09-17) which changed GTMHead/GoogleAnalytics/PageViewTracker, and with layout commits on 09-18/09-19. The GA4 ingestor pulls yesterday only with no settle window, and the silent-zero guard keys channel×metric with scopes collapsed, so a dead event stream can never trip it. Live fire test was blocked by the sandbox proxy, so the cause is a lead, not a verdict.
findings.evidence: ga4-daily-series.txt: 09-17 session_start 10, 09-18 1, 09-19..09-21 none; new_users 0 from 09-18; 08-19..08-31 identical; git show --stat f1e2a90f9 (GTMHead.tsx, GoogleAnalytics.tsx, PageViewTracker.tsx, VisitTracker.tsx, track route), 5d8a0f874 and 22b53b94a/3da4313bc (app/layout.tsx); lib/marketing-brain/snapshot.ts:124-138; scripts/loop-brief.ts:330-372 key `${channel}\u0000${metric}`; live-tags.txt (ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES).
findings.why_it_matters: The only consented, human GA4 signal (and Google Signals/audiences, offline-conversion matching) is dark again for the fourth week out of the last five, and nothing in the loop reports it; every GA4-based accept test on SITE nodes seeded in September is unmeasurable.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify in GA4 Realtime with a consented browser today; bisect f1e2a90f9 → 5d8a0f874 → 22b53b94a; then add (a) a settle window to the GA4 ingestor like GSC's, (b) a silent-zero watchlist keyed channel×scope×scope_id×metric with ga4:session_start and ga4:first_visit named explicitly, and (c) a Playwright gate in deploy:verify that loads / with a consent cookie and asserts one /g/collect page_view request.

findings.title: RUM is polluted: /_next/image misses render the full app 404 page, which reports vitals and page_views under path /_next/image (45% of LCP rows)
findings.claim: A missing image-optimizer URL returns HTTP 404 with the 142 KB application not-found page (root layout mounted), so WebVitalsReporter and VisitTracker fire with path /_next/image. In 14 days that one surface holds 20,306 of 45,354 LCP rows and 37,639 FCP rows, dilutes the 'other' class to p75 LCP 9.1 s, and leaks into visitor_events and GA4 page views. The reporter also has no sampling, no bot filter and no route normalization; INP has only 1,394 rows, and deprecated FID is still stored.
findings.evidence: curl -A Chrome '/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fdoes-not-exist-zz.jpg&w=640&q=75' → 404, 142,610 bytes, text/html; web_vitals rows path='/_next/image' navigation_type='navigate' (8 rows in 5 s on 09-22 19:45Z); site_signal rum 14d surface families (_next lcp 20,306; page lcp 25,048); visitor_events 12 rows in 7d with page_title 'Page not found' on /_next/image URLs; GA4 page scope /_next/image 34 views on 09-16; components/WebVitalsReporter.tsx; app/api/web-vitals/route.ts; app/layout.tsx:162.
findings.why_it_matters: Core Web Vitals are a visibility input the loop claims to measure; the per-route p75 the scoreboard shows is built on a table where the biggest 'page' is not a page, and every broken image also costs a full layout render on the server.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop samples whose path starts with /_next or /api in WebVitalsReporter and in /api/web-vitals; make the not-found route for /_next/image return a lightweight 404 (Next image route config or a middleware rule that answers non-HTML 404 for image-optimizer misses); store a page-class column (pageTypeFromPath) beside the raw path; stop storing FID; clamp absurd values; add a bot/UA check server-side. Then find the source of the /_next/image navigations (Spark CDN photo URLs at w=3840 suggest crawlers or open-in-new-tab) and fix the broken image references it reveals (e.g. /images/communities/broken-top.jpg).

findings.title: Organic search → identified person → lead attribution does not exist end to end; first-party 'direct' (98%) is unfiltered for bots and crm_people carries no channel
findings.claim: First-party capture stores referrer/UTMs at essential tier, but only 1.7% of 7-day sessions carry any referrer, 98.1% are 'direct', UA is stripped at essential tier, and neither /api/visitors/track nor middleware filters JS-rendering crawlers, so the denominator is untrustworthy. Of 90 people identified in 7 days, 1 is attributed to organic. crm_people has no channel/medium/first-touch columns; the attribution crons score only paid tags; the identity stitch writes a note, not a queryable field. Nobody can answer 'how many leads did search or AI referrals create this week'.
findings.evidence: db-reads.json §B (8,766 sessions: utm_medium none 8,600 / organic 146; user_agent present 218; identified 90, identifiedOrganic 1; fbclid/gclid 0); components/VisitTracker.tsx:79-160; app/api/visitors/track/route.ts:117-127,331 (no bot check); middleware.ts:150-171 GOOD_BOT_RE bypass; schema crm_people (source, source_url only); lib/crm/send-event.ts:77-84 (campaign param accepted but not forwarded); app/api/cron/buyer-lead-attribution/route.ts header (channel:*-ads only).
findings.why_it_matters: The mission is organic visibility that converts; without channel on the person there is no way to score what the loop ships against leads, and a bot-inflated 'direct' bucket hides whether search traffic is falling or rising.
findings.proposed_fix: At ensureNativeLead/identify time copy first-touch (utm_source/medium, referrer host, landing page, gclid/fbclid, first_seen_at) from visitor_sessions by rr_session_id onto crm_people (new columns or tags channel:organic/gbp/ai/email/direct), add an organic/AI branch to the attribution crons, store a server-side is_bot flag on visitor_sessions from UA + no-JS heuristics (keep UA hash even at essential tier or classify at write time), and report leads-by-channel weekly.

findings.title: GSC ingest cannot diagnose a per-page ranking loss: top-25 queries + top-25 pages per day, no page×query, no index coverage, no Bing
findings.claim: The daily GSC pull stores 25 queries and 25 pages by impressions; long-tail subdivision/neighborhood URLs (7,500-URL sitemap) never appear, absence is unknowable, target_query_benchmark is an ILIKE join on those rows, URL Inspection runs only by hand, and there is no Bing Webmaster or IndexNow integration.
findings.evidence: app/actions/search-console-report.ts:71-91 (rowLimit 1/25/25, dimensions ['query'] and ['page'] only); supabase/migrations/20260610230500_target_query_benchmark.sql (comment: absence ≠ zero); scripts/_gsc-index-check.mjs manual; grep indexnow → docs only; site_signal gsc page scope 1,543 distinct surfaces over 7 months.
findings.why_it_matters: Matt's question is 'why do we slip'; the stored search data can show the site-wide slope but not which page class or query lost, nor whether pages are indexed at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the GSC ingestor to pull page×query (and page×device) with rowLimit 25,000 + startRow pagination for the last settled day into a dedicated table keyed by page class; add a weekly URL Inspection sample (2,000/day quota) writing indexed/not-indexed per class; add Bing Webmaster API pull; make target_query_benchmark exact-match on the full pull.

findings.title: Three different 'conversion' definitions (18 in docs, 7 in ga4-admin, 9 in the report) and server-fired generate_lead with no session context
findings.claim: docs/ANALYTICS_LEAD_TRACKING.md lists 18 GA4 conversion events, scripts/ga4-admin.mjs declares 7, app/actions/ga4-report.ts counts 9 LEAD_EVENT_NAMES for total_lead_events/lead_event_rate; generate_lead (135 in 14d) is fired from the server without a session, so 156 of 161 lead events carry lead_source '(not set)'.
findings.evidence: docs/ANALYTICS_LEAD_TRACKING.md:117-119; scripts/ga4-admin.mjs:78-86; app/actions/ga4-report.ts:6-16; lib/lead-tracking.ts:77-115; site_signal ga4 event/lead_source 14d sums.

findings.proposed_fix: One exported CONVERSION_EVENTS module consumed by ga4-admin apply/audit, the report, and the docs (generated), with the primary conversion named; have fireLeadGenerated pass the rr_session_id-derived client_id and the first-touch source captured in visitor_sessions.

findings.title: Dead and dormant feeds still count as healthy: fub_api_v1 rows remain in site_signal, meta-ads stays in the fan-out writing nothing, and children never log rows written
findings.claim: fub_api_v1 (1,228 rows, last 06-23; system decommissioned 06-24) is still unioned into site_signal; meta_ads_insights_api has written nothing since 06-19 yet snapshot-channels reports it ok daily because only the roll-up logs; tiktok video (05-12) and x post (08-16) are 30-day lookback feeds on idle accounts; ga4 channel scope writes only on days with social sessions. A reader sees 8/8 green and cannot tell measured-zero from not-measured.
findings.evidence: site_signal freshness table (notes.md §1); app/api/cron/snapshot-channels/route.ts:59-91 (children not logged); marketing-snapshot-tiktok/route.ts:226-231; marketing-snapshot-x/route.ts:158-163; marketing-snapshot-ga4/route.ts:151-168; sync_logs 200/8 daily.

findings.title: Speed-to-lead is flagged per person but never stored as a metric; 11 of the 15 most recent site submits had no human touch in 24 hours
findings.claim: The response clock correctly defines a human touch and flags leads at 5 minutes and 24 hours on crm_people.custom, but no median/percentile or unanswered count is written to marketing_channel_daily/site_signal, so neither the scoreboard, the silent-zero guard nor the loop brief can see that follow-up is failing. The most recent 15 flagged site leads (09-20..09-22) all hit the 5-minute flag and 11 hit the 24-hour flag; human outbound in 14 days is 6 calls, 5 SMS, 124 Gmail emails against 153 leads created.
findings.evidence: db-reads.json §C (15 rows custom->response_clock); §D crm_timeline 14d kinds (call 6, voicemail 2, sms_out 5, sms_in 1, email_out gmail 124/app 91/sequence 74, lead_created 153, system/response-clock 146); lib/crm/response-clock-run.ts:12-14,39-50; app/api/cron/crm-response-clock/route.ts.
findings.why_it_matters: Being seen only pays if the lead is answered; the one number that proves conversion is happening (or not) is invisible to the process that decides what to build next.

findings.title: No per-lead SMS consent record is persisted (TRACKING_POLICY backlog #3 still open) while sequences send SMS
findings.claim: The disclosure is shown (ci:sms-consent) but no table or column records consent text version, scope, timestamp or IP per lead; crm_people has only a phones jsonb; sms_out rows exist (5 in 14d, one from a sequence).
findings.evidence: docs/TRACKING_POLICY.md:108-113; DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md: no *consent* table, crm_people has only `phones`; db-reads.json §D sms_out 5 (app 4, sequence 1).
findings.why_it_matters: State mini-TCPA exposure for a licensed broker; and without a consent record the SMS channel cannot be safely scaled as a follow-up lever.
findings.proposed_fix: Add crm_consent_records (person_id, channel, scope, text_version, granted_at, ip, source_url) written by every form that collects a phone, and have the sequence engine refuse SMS without a matching row.

findings.title: GBP review velocity is not measured by any cron
findings.claim: The GBP snapshot stores 9 performance metrics with a correct 10-day lag window, but reviews (count, rating, velocity) — a map-pack ranking input — are only pulled by a manual script; the route carries a TODO.
findings.evidence: app/api/cron/marketing-snapshot-gbp/route.ts:22-27 (TODO: review ingestion not handled); scripts/ingest-gbp-reviews.mjs (manual); site_signal gbp_performance_api_v1 9 metrics.
findings.why_it_matters: Local visibility for 'Bend real estate agents' style queries depends on review count and recency; nobody sees when it stalls.
findings.proposed_fix: Add review count/average/new-reviews-7d to the GBP ingestor (same OAuth token, /reviews endpoint) as marketing_channel_daily rows and to the scoreboard.

findings.title: No measured signal enters prioritization: the loop brief reads marketing_channel_daily only for the silent-zero guard, nodes are hand-pasted, and the weekly scoreboard is five weeks stale
findings.claim: site_signal, GSC, GA4, RUM and social feeds are ingested but none is consumed by loop-brief or seed-site-queue to rank work; COMPANY_SCOREBOARD.md says 'overwrite weekly' and reads 'Week of 2026-08-15'; the ledger has 8 open windows and 7 expired-unlearned. A ranking loss today has no automatic path to a node.
findings.evidence: scripts/loop-brief.ts:330-372 (only silent-zero); scripts/seed-site-queue.ts:11-14; docs/plans/COMPANY_SCOREBOARD.md:9; scoreboard-probe.txt ledger (rows 20, openWindows 8, expiredUnlearned 7).
findings.why_it_matters: The loop cannot be recursive if measurement never feeds selection; every 'measure → learn' promise in DEVELOPMENT_PROCESS.md is currently manual and unrun.
findings.proposed_fix: A weekly measurer job (cron or routine) that overwrites the scoreboard from the probe plus a per-page-class GSC/RUM/lead table and emits candidate nodes (class, delta, evidence) into loop_work_nodes in 'proposed' state; the brief prints the top three deltas before any node list.
